html:
The Yavapai are a Native American people of west-central Arizona, who once held some 10 million acres between the San Francisco Peaks, the Colorado River and the Salt and Gila rivers.

They speak an Upland Yuman language, close to that of the Havasupai and Hualapai. They lived in four bands, gathering mesquite, agave and acorns, hunting, and farming small plots. Settlers often confused them with their Apache neighbours, with whom some bands lived and married.

After gold was found in their land in the 1860s, the US Army fought them, and in 1875 forced about 1,500 Yavapai and Apache to march in winter from the Verde Valley to the San Carlos reservation. Many died. Some returned decades later. Today there are three Yavapai tribes, including the Yavapai-Apache Nation.
sum: The Yavapai are a Native American people of west-central Arizona, who once held some 10 million acres between the San Francisco Peaks, the Colorado River and the Salt and Gila rivers.
